gaps: The promise that agents cannot merge or commit to the default branch has no server-side enforcement plan. Local hooks and a required check do not restrict who may push or merge; branch protection and actor permissions are unspecified (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:25; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:339; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

The plan promises to measure factory performance but assigns no owner or proof for the spec’s three success measures: median task cycle time, human touches, and the share of PRs fixing Forge. Step durations and slow flags alone do not establish those results or the check date (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:29; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:79; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:794).

Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The source commits, destination modules, and proof that this work survives the switch are unstated (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:44; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:54).

The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. STORY owns that command before the fix and close lanes exist, but the plan gives no branch, PR, review, and CI sequence for its state write (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:177; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:188; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:288; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612).

The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. Archiving the whole directory would include the destination or newly written v1 state (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:303; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:406).

DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. The plan does not say whether the tag is created after that merge or how the release is checked against the final default-branch tree (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:400; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:410; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:566).

A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. The plan needs a review-freshness rule for delivery-changing doc edits before merge (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:275; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400).
contradictions: The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files. Today’s degraded window is a Claude companion outage exception, and its stage-close fallback counts at most five total in-scope files, including tests and Markdown. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).

The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).

CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. The confirmed spec requires exactly one test function per numbered criterion, so the stated per-task proof assignments cannot all hold as written (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:166; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:192; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:381; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:592).

STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The old contract binds the current semantic plan digest, and decision 0093 explicitly drops its old digest and eligibility rules. The plan must specify the new digest and trust behavior rather than promise an unchanged port (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:181; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/plan-approval.md:48; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:117).

SETUP makes the first commit on the default branch and then runs `forge sync`, which writes generated adapter files. The spec permits only init’s first commit on that branch and says sync changes land only on a branch; as ordered, a fresh repo is left with default-branch changes that its new hooks refuse to commit (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:253; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:256; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:617).

BOARD is marked `user_facing: false` even though it creates `board.html` and changes the page read by a person. The v1 close contract requires a functional check for a user-facing task, so this classification skips required proof (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:273; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:422; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:263; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:681).

MIGRATE writes a fix state and deletes many code files, yet WORK’s hooks and CLOSE’s PR check reject a fix beyond five code files without `allow-large`. No migration exception or recorded human permission is assigned, so the promised one-PR migration cannot pass its own gates as planned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:220; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:294; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306).

DOCS-STANDARDS says criterion 37 passes before DOCS-PHASES, but criterion 37 requires motion-skill wording in the brief and review text, and DOCS-PHASES is the task assigned to write those texts. The claimed completion order is impossible (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:337; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:350; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:356; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:772).

ADOPT carries the warm-threads approval over unchanged although its approved delivery promises `.envrc` hybrid/Codex/Claude modes and `forge upgrade`, while v1 ships a `forge.toml` Claude worker setting, refuses Codex workers, and replaces upgrade with pin-and-sync. These are changes to `What changes for you` and `Done when`, which require fresh approval (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:16; plans/active/FORGE-WARM-1-hybrid-mode-reuses-warm-codex-worker-threads.md:28; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:57; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:220; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174).

ADOPT replaces hooks but leaves the old source-repo instructions outside any generated Forge block. `AGENTS.md` still directs agents to the old `./forge`, constitution, proof files, and plugin route; `forge sync` is required to preserve text outside its block. The source repo would give incompatible instructions while running v1 and after SWITCH deletes their targets (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:369; AGENTS.md:23; AGENTS.md:75; AGENTS.md:90; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:366).

The FDE pilot is required to complete before SWITCH while the old tree stays untouched until SWITCH. The FDE story’s Done-when requires removing gstack from this repo’s old code, settings, living docs, and tests; it cannot finish that contract while those files remain untouched (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:134; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:121; plans/active/FORGE-FDE-1-the-agent-works-as-a-forward-deployed-engineer-gstack-removed.md:35).

SWITCH deletes every doc outside the guide, standards, specs, and decisions, including `docs/archive.md` that DOCS-STANDARDS has just delivered and the FDE pilot’s `docs/context/gstack-archive/` and `docs/product/DISCOVERY.md`. The plan does not reconcile those promised outputs with the deletion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:332; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:397; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:39; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:95).

The task table marks STORY, RECORDS, WORK, CLOSE, SETUP, MIGRATE, and ADOPT as covering Done-when items that require later real-world checks. For example MIGRATE claims item 3 before myclaw’s PR and subsequent fix, and CLOSE claims item 2 before a fresh client exists. Since only covered items may block review, these Covers values misstate what those tasks can deliver (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:51; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:52; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:420; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:423; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:127).

SWITCH’s prose requires all three switch checks, but its task-table dependency is only ADOPT. The recorded graph therefore permits SWITCH to start before the FDE pilot, fresh-client fix, or myclaw migration and fix complete (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:427; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:558).
resolutions: Server-side: branch protection on main requires a PR, the required checks (tests + forge-pr-check) and no direct pushes; SETUP applies it to clients via `gh api` (reported, not silent), SWITCH to this repo; the deny hook blocks `gh pr merge` for agents.
Success measures: BOARD computes the three metrics from state + GitHub; a `forge next` line shows them after the check date; owner of the check-back is the coordinator on 2026-11-15.

Harvest: PILOT-FDE ports FDE's skill text and payback code (branch feat/FORGE-FDE-1-FDE, commit a529a1ee); SDK-SETUP code (branch feat/FORGE-WARM-1-SDK-SETUP) is harvested by the WARM re-plan after the switch; both branches kept.
Bootstrap: `forge init`/`migrate` write forge.toml pinned to the running version; ADOPT installs the rc tag it just created (tag after its PR merges) and pins it.
This plan gets its `New moving parts:` line now: the v1 package, state files, git hooks, host adapters, CI workflow, migrate — each tied to its Done-when item; ADOPT's conversion keeps it.
`story done` writes its outcome through a fix it opens itself (kind story-done), closed like any fix; it lands in CLOSE's lane after CLOSE merges (STORY defines the command, CLOSE wires the fix).
CLOSE acceptance lists explicit tests: failed/incomplete Autoreview → one retry then refuse; missing required check → not green; GitHub API error → not green with reason.
forge-pr-check runs the checker from the base branch (pull_request_target with base checkout, like today's ticket gate) and reads policy/config from base; PR head is data only.
SETUP makes forge-pr-check and tests required via branch protection in the client it initialises; MIGRATE does the same for migrated clients (reported in the PR).

MIGRATE refuses unless the working tree is clean; it owns `forge/migrate-v1` only if its state file marks it Forge-created; if the branch has commits not made by migrate it stops and asks (never resets user work).
Archive = every pre-migration `.factory/` entry except `archive/`, moved first to `.factory/archive/pre-v1-<date>/`; then the migrate fix state is written; collisions add a numeric suffix.
Standards and templates ship inside the package (`src/forge/standards.md`, `src/forge/templates/`); SETUP adds an installed-from-tag test that opens them in a fresh client.
ADOPT converts only the plans that exist (FDE, WARM); the sign-off story has no plan in this checkout — remove that claim.

Switch checks become tasks: PILOT-FDE (after ADOPT), CLIENT-FIX (fresh client, after SETUP+CLOSE+WORK), MIGRATE-MYCLAW (after MIGRATE+ADOPT, external repo; acceptance = merged migrate PR + one merged fix in myclaw). SWITCH depends on all three.
SWITCH's tag v1.0.0 is created after its PR merges, on the merge commit, with a check that the tag tree equals main.
Review freshness counts the story doc's Tasks/Risks/New moving parts as reviewed content: a change to them after a clean review needs a new review round.

Wording: Claude writers use Forge's ledgered Claude-writer path (degraded windows) by owner instruction, temporarily, until v1's own worker runs this repo after ADOPT; the hook budget counts code files (tests and Markdown excluded); tasks are closed by PR, not stage close.
Command ceiling counts top-level commands; `payback` and `measure` are subcommands of `forge spec`; the re-planned FDE story uses those names.
Exactly one test per criterion: assign each criterion's test to one task; other tasks reference it.

STORY defines v1 approval: hash of "What changes for you" + "Done when"; Codex capture keeps today's trust checks (exact digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal, one eligible candidate) applied to that hash.
`forge init` makes one first commit containing both the scaffold and sync output; later syncs land on a branch.
BOARD is user_facing: true (functional check).
Migrate fix state carries `allow-large` set by the human who runs `forge migrate` (recorded with their name).
Criterion 37 moves to DOCS-PHASES.
WARM is not carried over; it is re-planned after the switch (fresh approval). ADOPT marks it "needs re-plan".
ADOPT regenerates AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md with the v1 block and replaces old instructions outside it (this repo only; clients keep their text).

FDE is re-planned for v1 before PILOT-FDE (one fresh FDE approval): its gstack-removal task is dropped as moot (SWITCH deletes the old tree); pilot scope = skill, payback, spec measure, impeccable row.
SWITCH keeps docs/archive.md, docs/product/, docs/context/ and every doc the pilot produced; only old Forge docs are deleted.
Covers columns list only the items each task can finish; real-world items (2, 3) are covered by CLIENT-FIX and MIGRATE-MYCLAW.
SWITCH depends on ADOPT, PILOT-FDE, CLIENT-FIX, MIGRATE-MYCLAW.

Today’s degraded window is a Claude companion outage exception, and its stage-close fallback counts at most five total in-scope files, including tests and Markdown. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).
finding_dispositions.resolution: Wording: Claude writers use Forge's ledgered Claude-writer path (degraded windows) by owner instruction, temporarily, until v1's own worker runs this repo after ADOPT; the hook budget counts code files (tests and Markdown excluded); tasks are closed by PR, not stage close.

finding_dispositions.finding: The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).
finding_dispositions.resolution: Command ceiling counts top-level commands; `payback` and `measure` are subcommands of `forge spec`; the re-planned FDE story uses those names.

finding_dispositions.finding: CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. The confirmed spec requires exactly one test function per numbered criterion, so the stated per-task proof assignments cannot all hold as written (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:166; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:192; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:381; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:592).
finding_dispositions.resolution: Exactly one test per criterion: assign each criterion's test to one task; other tasks reference it.

finding_dispositions.finding: STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The old contract binds the current semantic plan digest, and decision 0093 explicitly drops its old digest and eligibility rules. The plan must specify the new digest and trust behavior rather than promise an unchanged port (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:181; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/plan-approval.md:48; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:117).
finding_dispositions.resolution: STORY defines v1 approval: hash of "What changes for you" + "Done when"; Codex capture keeps today's trust checks (exact digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal, one eligible candidate) applied to that hash.

finding_dispositions.finding: SETUP makes the first commit on the default branch and then runs `forge sync`, which writes generated adapter files. The spec permits only init’s first commit on that branch and says sync changes land only on a branch; as ordered, a fresh repo is left with default-branch changes that its new hooks refuse to commit (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:253; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:256; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:617).
finding_dispositions.resolution: `forge init` makes one first commit containing both the scaffold and sync output; later syncs land on a branch.

finding_dispositions.finding: BOARD is marked `user_facing: false` even though it creates `board.html` and changes the page read by a person. The v1 close contract requires a functional check for a user-facing task, so this classification skips required proof (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:273; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:422; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:263; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:681).
finding_dispositions.resolution: BOARD is user_facing: true (functional check).

finding_dispositions.finding: MIGRATE writes a fix state and deletes many code files, yet WORK’s hooks and CLOSE’s PR check reject a fix beyond five code files without `allow-large`. No migration exception or recorded human permission is assigned, so the promised one-PR migration cannot pass its own gates as planned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:220; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:294; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306).
finding_dispositions.resolution: Migrate fix state carries `allow-large` set by the human who runs `forge migrate` (recorded with their name).

finding_dispositions.finding: DOCS-STANDARDS says criterion 37 passes before DOCS-PHASES, but criterion 37 requires motion-skill wording in the brief and review text, and DOCS-PHASES is the task assigned to write those texts. The claimed completion order is impossible (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:337; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:350; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:356; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:772).
finding_dispositions.resolution: Criterion 37 moves to DOCS-PHASES.

finding_dispositions.finding: ADOPT carries the warm-threads approval over unchanged although its approved delivery promises `.envrc` hybrid/Codex/Claude modes and `forge upgrade`, while v1 ships a `forge.toml` Claude worker setting, refuses Codex workers, and replaces upgrade with pin-and-sync. finding_dispositions.resolution: WARM is not carried over; it is re-planned after the switch (fresh approval). ADOPT marks it "needs re-plan".

finding_dispositions.finding: ADOPT replaces hooks but leaves the old source-repo instructions outside any generated Forge block. `AGENTS.md` still directs agents to the old `./forge`, constitution, proof files, and plugin route; `forge sync` is required to preserve text outside its block. The source repo would give incompatible instructions while running v1 and after SWITCH deletes their targets (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:369; AGENTS.md:23; AGENTS.md:75; AGENTS.md:90; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:366).
finding_dispositions.resolution: ADOPT regenerates AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md with the v1 block and replaces old instructions outside it (this repo only; clients keep their text).

finding_dispositions.finding: The FDE pilot is required to complete before SWITCH while the old tree stays untouched until SWITCH. finding_dispositions.resolution: FDE is re-planned for v1 before PILOT-FDE (one fresh FDE approval): its gstack-removal task is dropped as moot (SWITCH deletes the old tree); pilot scope = skill, payback, spec measure, impeccable row.

finding_dispositions.finding: SWITCH deletes every doc outside the guide, standards, specs, and decisions, including `docs/archive.md` that DOCS-STANDARDS has just delivered and the FDE pilot’s `docs/context/gstack-archive/` and `docs/product/DISCOVERY.md`. finding_dispositions.resolution: SWITCH keeps docs/archive.md, docs/product/, docs/context/ and every doc the pilot produced; only old Forge docs are deleted.

finding_dispositions.finding: The task table marks STORY, RECORDS, WORK, CLOSE, SETUP, MIGRATE, and ADOPT as covering Done-when items that require later real-world checks. finding_dispositions.resolution: Covers columns list only the items each task can finish; real-world items (2, 3) are covered by CLIENT-FIX and MIGRATE-MYCLAW.

finding_dispositions.finding: SWITCH’s prose requires all three switch checks, but its task-table dependency is only ADOPT. SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. The plan needs a review-freshness rule for delivery-changing doc edits before merge (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:275; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400).

The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).

The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).

CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).

CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. The confirmed spec requires exactly one test function per numbered criterion, so the stated per-task proof assignments cannot all hold as written (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:166; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:192; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:381; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:592).

STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The old contract binds the current semantic plan digest, and decision 0093 explicitly drops its old digest and eligibility rules. The plan must specify the new digest and trust behavior rather than promise an unchanged port (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:181; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/plan-approval.md:48; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:117).

SETUP makes the first commit on the default branch and then runs `forge sync`, which writes generated adapter files. The spec permits only init’s first commit on that branch and says sync changes land only on a branch; as ordered, a fresh repo is left with default-branch changes that its new hooks refuse to commit (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:253; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:256; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:617).

BOARD is marked `user_facing: false` even though it creates `board.html` and changes the page read by a person. MIGRATE writes a fix state and deletes many code files, yet WORK’s hooks and CLOSE’s PR check reject a fix beyond five code files without `allow-large`. The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. ADOPT replaces hooks but leaves the old source-repo instructions outside any generated Forge block. `AGENTS.md` still directs agents to the old `./forge`, constitution, proof files, and plugin route; `forge sync` is required to preserve text outside its block. The source repo would give incompatible instructions while running v1 and after SWITCH deletes their targets (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:369; AGENTS.md:23; AGENTS.md:75; AGENTS.md:90; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:366).

The FDE pilot is required to complete before SWITCH while the old tree stays untouched until SWITCH. The FDE story’s Done-when requires removing gstack from this repo’s old code, settings, living docs, and tests; it cannot finish that contract while those files remain untouched (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:134; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:121; plans/active/FORGE-FDE-1-the-agent-works-as-a-forward-deployed-engineer-gstack-removed.md:35).

SWITCH deletes every doc outside the guide, standards, specs, and decisions, including `docs/archive.md` that DOCS-STANDARDS has just delivered and the FDE pilot’s `docs/context/gstack-archive/` and `docs/product/DISCOVERY.md`. The plan does not reconcile those promised outputs with the deletion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:332; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:397; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:39; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:95).

The task table marks STORY, RECORDS, WORK, CLOSE, SETUP, MIGRATE, and ADOPT as covering Done-when items that require later real-world checks. For example MIGRATE claims item 3 before myclaw’s PR and subsequent fix, and CLOSE claims item 2 before a fresh client exists. Since only covered items may block review, these Covers values misstate what those tasks can deliver (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:51; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:52; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:420; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:423; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:127).

SWITCH’s prose requires all three switch checks, but its task-table dependency is only ADOPT. The recorded graph therefore permits SWITCH to start before the FDE pilot, fresh-client fix, or myclaw migration and fix complete (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:427; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:558).

findings: The promise that agents cannot merge or commit to the default branch has no server-side enforcement plan. Local hooks and a required check do not restrict who may push or merge; branch protection and actor permissions are unspecified (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:25; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:339; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

The plan promises to measure factory performance but assigns no owner or proof for the spec’s three success measures: median task cycle time, human touches, and the share of PRs fixing Forge. Step durations and slow flags alone do not establish those results or the check date (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:29; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:79; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:794).

Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The source commits, destination modules, and proof that this work survives the switch are unstated (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:44; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:54).

The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. STORY owns that command before the fix and close lanes exist, but the plan gives no branch, PR, review, and CI sequence for its state write (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:177; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:188; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:288; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612).

The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. Archiving the whole directory would include the destination or newly written v1 state (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:303; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:406).

DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. The plan does not say whether the tag is created after that merge or how the release is checked against the final default-branch tree (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:400; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:410; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:566).

A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. The plan needs a review-freshness rule for delivery-changing doc edits before merge (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:275; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400).

The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files. Today’s degraded window is a Claude companion outage exception, and its stage-close fallback counts at most five total in-scope files, including tests and Markdown. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).

The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).

CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The old contract binds the current semantic plan digest, and decision 0093 explicitly drops its old digest and eligibility rules. The plan must specify the new digest and trust behavior rather than promise an unchanged port (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:181; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/plan-approval.md:48; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:117).

findings: The promise that agents cannot merge or commit to the default branch has no server-side enforcement plan. The plan promises to measure factory performance but assigns no owner or proof for the spec’s three success measures: median task cycle time, human touches, and the share of PRs fixing Forge. Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The source commits, destination modules, and proof that this work survives the switch are unstated (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:44; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:54).

The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. STORY owns that command before the fix and close lanes exist, but the plan gives no branch, PR, review, and CI sequence for its state write (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:177; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:188; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:288; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612).

The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. findings: The promise that agents cannot merge or commit to the default branch has no server-side enforcement plan. The plan promises to measure factory performance but assigns no owner or proof for the spec’s three success measures: median task cycle time, human touches, and the share of PRs fixing Forge. Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. findings: The promise that agents cannot merge or commit to the default branch has no server-side enforcement plan. Local hooks and a required check do not restrict who may push or merge; branch protection and actor permissions are unspecified (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:25; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:339; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

The plan promises to measure factory performance but assigns no owner or proof for the spec’s three success measures: median task cycle time, human touches, and the share of PRs fixing Forge. Step durations and slow flags alone do not establish those results or the check date (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:29; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:79; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:794).

Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The source commits, destination modules, and proof that this work survives the switch are unstated (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:44; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:54).

The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. STORY owns that command before the fix and close lanes exist, but the plan gives no branch, PR, review, and CI sequence for its state write (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:177; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:188; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:288; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612).

The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. Archiving the whole directory would include the destination or newly written v1 state (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:303; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:406).

DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. The plan needs a review-freshness rule for delivery-changing doc edits before merge (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:275; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400).

The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files. Today’s degraded window is a Claude companion outage exception, and its stage-close fallback counts at most five total in-scope files, including tests and Markdown. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).

The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. SWITCH’s prose requires all three switch checks, but its task-table dependency is only ADOPT. findings: The promise that agents cannot merge or commit to the default branch has no server-side enforcement plan. Local hooks and a required check do not restrict who may push or merge; branch protection and actor permissions are unspecified (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:25; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:339; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

The plan promises to measure factory performance but assigns no owner or proof for the spec’s three success measures: median task cycle time, human touches, and the share of PRs fixing Forge. Step durations and slow flags alone do not establish those results or the check date (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:29; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:79; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:794).

Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The source commits, destination modules, and proof that this work survives the switch are unstated (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:44; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:54).

The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. STORY owns that command before the fix and close lanes exist, but the plan gives no branch, PR, review, and CI sequence for its state write (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:177; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:188; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:288; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612).

The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. Archiving the whole directory would include the destination or newly written v1 state (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:303; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:406).

DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. The plan does not say whether the tag is created after that merge or how the release is checked against the final default-branch tree (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:400; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:410; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:566).

A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. The plan needs a review-freshness rule for delivery-changing doc edits before merge (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:275; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400).

The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files. Today’s degraded window is a Claude companion outage exception, and its stage-close fallback counts at most five total in-scope files, including tests and Markdown. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).

The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).

CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. The confirmed spec requires exactly one test function per numbered criterion, so the stated per-task proof assignments cannot all hold as written (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:166; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:192; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:381; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:592).

STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The old contract binds the current semantic plan digest, and decision 0093 explicitly drops its old digest and eligibility rules. The plan must specify the new digest and trust behavior rather than promise an unchanged port (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:181; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/plan-approval.md:48; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:117).

SETUP makes the first commit on the default branch and then runs `forge sync`, which writes generated adapter files. The spec permits only init’s first commit on that branch and says sync changes land only on a branch; as ordered, a fresh repo is left with default-branch changes that its new hooks refuse to commit (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:253; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:256; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:617).

BOARD is marked `user_facing: false` even though it creates `board.html` and changes the page read by a person. The v1 close contract requires a functional check for a user-facing task, so this classification skips required proof (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:273; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:422; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:263; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:681).

MIGRATE writes a fix state and deletes many code files, yet WORK’s hooks and CLOSE’s PR check reject a fix beyond five code files without `allow-large`. No migration exception or recorded human permission is assigned, so the promised one-PR migration cannot pass its own gates as planned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:220; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:294; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306).

DOCS-STANDARDS says criterion 37 passes before DOCS-PHASES, but criterion 37 requires motion-skill wording in the brief and review text, and DOCS-PHASES is the task assigned to write those texts. The claimed completion order is impossible (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:337; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:350; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:356; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:772).

ADOPT carries the warm-threads approval over unchanged although its approved delivery promises `.envrc` hybrid/Codex/Claude modes and `forge upgrade`, while v1 ships a `forge.toml` Claude worker setting, refuses Codex workers, and replaces upgrade with pin-and-sync. ADOPT replaces hooks but leaves the old source-repo instructions outside any generated Forge block. `AGENTS.md` still directs agents to the old `./forge`, constitution, proof files, and plugin route; `forge sync` is required to preserve text outside its block. The source repo would give incompatible instructions while running v1 and after SWITCH deletes their targets (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:369; AGENTS.md:23; AGENTS.md:75; AGENTS.md:90; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:366).

Decision 0093 requires already built FDE and SDK setup code to carry into v1, but the freeze and ADOPT steps name only plan conversion. The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The version-pin rule has no bootstrap path for `forge init` or `forge migrate`, which run before a repo has `forge.toml`. ADOPT also needs a matching installed release before it tags `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the plan does not name that version or installation sequence (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:158; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:377; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:54; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:72).

The draft has no `New moving parts:` declaration tying its new package, state, hooks, CI, and migration machinery to Done-when items. ADOPT says it converts this plan into a v1 story doc, but neither the conversion nor a validation step supplies the required line before the first task PR (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:171; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:132; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:753).

`story done` must record an outcome through a Forge-made fix after the last task merges. STORY owns that command before the fix and close lanes exist, but the plan gives no branch, PR, review, and CI sequence for its state write (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:177; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:188; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:288; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612).

The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. Archiving the whole directory would include the destination or newly written v1 state (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:303; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:406).

DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

SWITCH says to tag `v1.0.0` as part of its task, but each task still ships by a human-merged PR. The plan does not say whether the tag is created after that merge or how the release is checked against the final default-branch tree (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:400; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:410; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:566).

A clean review can remain authoritative after an unreviewed edit to the story’s Tasks, Risks, Notes, or `New moving parts`: approval binds only two sections, while review freshness excludes `plans/` from the product tree. The plan needs a review-freshness rule for delivery-changing doc edits before merge (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:275; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400).

The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files. Today’s degraded window is a Claude companion outage exception, and its stage-close fallback counts at most five total in-scope files, including tests and Markdown. It does not authorize the stated normal task route or file accounting (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:94; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:102; docs/degraded-mode.md:39; docs/degraded-mode.md:46; docs/degraded-mode.md:52; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:1663).

The immutable 20-command table has no slots for the FDE pilot’s required `forge payback` and `forge spec measure`. That pilot must finish before SWITCH, while the rules check refuses more than 20 commands and raising the ceiling needs an accepted decision (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:135; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:163; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:386; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:65; docs/specs/fde-discovery.md:78; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:597).

CORE, STORY, and ADOPT each claim criterion 4 test ownership, and criteria 2 and 7 are likewise claimed across tasks. The confirmed spec requires exactly one test function per numbered criterion, so the stated per-task proof assignments cannot all hold as written (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:166; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:192; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:381; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:592).

STORY says it ports the old plan-approval contract unchanged, but v1 changes the approval boundary to a hash of only `What changes for you` and `Done when`. The old contract binds the current semantic plan digest, and decision 0093 explicitly drops its old digest and eligibility rules. The plan must specify the new digest and trust behavior rather than promise an unchanged port (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:181; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:174; docs/specs/plan-approval.md:48; docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:117).

SETUP makes the first commit on the default branch and then runs `forge sync`, which writes generated adapter files. The spec permits only init’s first commit on that branch and says sync changes land only on a branch; as ordered, a fresh repo is left with default-branch changes that its new hooks refuse to commit (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:253; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:256; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:612; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:617).

BOARD is marked `user_facing: false` even though it creates `board.html` and changes the page read by a person. The v1 close contract requires a functional check for a user-facing task, so this classification skips required proof (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:273; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:422; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:263; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:681).

MIGRATE writes a fix state and deletes many code files, yet WORK’s hooks and CLOSE’s PR check reject a fix beyond five code files without `allow-large`. DOCS-STANDARDS says criterion 37 passes before DOCS-PHASES, but criterion 37 requires motion-skill wording in the brief and review text, and DOCS-PHASES is the task assigned to write those texts. The claimed completion order is impossible (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:337; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:350; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:356; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:772).

ADOPT carries the warm-threads approval over unchanged although its approved delivery promises `.envrc` hybrid/Codex/Claude modes and `forge upgrade`, while v1 ships a `forge.toml` Claude worker setting, refuses Codex workers, and replaces upgrade with pin-and-sync. The CLOSE task has no explicit acceptance proof for failed or incomplete Autoreview output, a missing required check, or a GitHub API error. The close contract requires one retry then a refusal for failed review, and treats missing checks or API errors as not green; a generic claim that applicable criteria pass leaves these failure paths unassigned (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:229; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:248; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:83; docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:93).

The plan does not say which trusted revision supplies `forge-pr-check` policy and configuration on a PR. If the job executes checker code or a version pin from the proposed head, the same PR can weaken its required gate. The current ticket gate deliberately checks out base code before judging PR data (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:240; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:18; .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:54).

SETUP generates a `forge-pr-check` job, but no step makes it required in a fresh client or myclaw before their switch-check fixes. SWITCH makes the check required only in this source repo, so those client PRs could merge without the promised backstop (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:260; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:393; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:392).

MIGRATE says an interrupted run resets `forge/migrate-v1`, but does not require a clean target, establish ownership of an existing branch, or preserve work made after interruption. Resetting that branch can discard client changes; preflight must distinguish Forge’s partial run from user work (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:291; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:496; docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:39).

MIGRATE does not define which legacy `.factory/` entries move into `.factory/archive/`, collision handling, or ordering against creation of the new migrate fix state. Archiving the whole directory would include the destination or newly written v1 state (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:303; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:306; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:406).

DOCS-STANDARDS keeps `docs/standards.md` outside `src/forge/` while promising it is shipped inside the installed package and included in every worker brief. The plan needs an installed-from-tag test that opens the packaged standards and Markdown templates from a fresh client (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:318; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:338; docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:49).

ADOPT says it converts the sign-off plan, but this checkout has active FDE and warm-thread plans and no sign-off story or plan to convert. The roadmap entry for FORGE-NEXT-1 is followed by the end of the story list; the plan must identify the actual sign-off artifact or remove the claimed conversion (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:367; plans/roadmap.json:1099; plans/roadmap.json:1116).

The three real switch checks are prose between ADOPT and SWITCH, with no owners, worktree scopes, dependencies, or acceptance records in the task graph. In particular, the fresh-client fix and myclaw migration and fix are external-repo work that the MIGRATE fixture test does not perform (plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:312; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:384; plans/FORGE-NEXT-1-draft.md:408).

The normal implementation route is specified as Claude Opus subagents inside degraded windows, counting only five code files.
